messages.content: No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. In the USA, if a copyright infringement case has been decided by the judicial system to be fair use, is it more accurate to say that a) copyright infringement occurred but it was legally excused, or b) copyright infringement did not occur?

message.content: b) copyright infringement did not occur. In the US, fair use is a statutory defense. If a court decides fair use, the use is not an infringement. This is not a pardon for a completed wrong; it means the alleged wrong is not legally infringement. Some opinions describe fair use as defeating a prima facie case, yet the final legal outcome remains non-infringement.
